newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says may cut data supply to CME, SIMEX.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says may cut data supply to CME, SIMEX.

text.p: Taiwan regulators said on Saturday they did not rule out the possibility of cutting data supply to futures exchanges in Chicago and Singapore after a six-month review.
Regulators said they would postpone the planned establishment of a domestic futures exchange to January 1998 from the scheduled October 1997.

"If local securities brokerage houses drastically opposed the Chicago and Singapore exchanges' move, we do not rule out the possibility to cut data supply to the two exchanges," an official quoted the Securities and Exchange Commission chairman Lu Tung-ying as saying.
"But we will at least wait a period of six months to evaluate whether to do so (cut the data supply) or to legalise their (Chicago and Singapore exchanges') products," Lu said.
The Chicago Mercantile Exchange and Singapore International Monetary Exchange said recently that they would launch Taiwan stock index-linked futures from January 9, 1997.

The commission, which is overseeing the development of Taiwan's own futures exchange, has faced heavy pressure to accelerate the domestic exchange's establishment after the CME and SIMEX announcements.

But Lu was quoted as saying that because of the failure by parliament to complete legislation of the Futures Trading Law by the end of 1996, the scheduled establishment of a domestic futures exchange would be postponed to January 1998 at the earliest.

The commission had hoped the two overseas exchanges would delay the start of their Taiwan index-futures until the simultaneous introduction of domestic Taiwan stock index-futures, but the two have insisted they would go ahead.

Another commission executive in December said the commission would wait until CME and SIMEX launched their Taiwan stock-index futures in January before deciding whether to cooperate with -- or seek to block -- the projects.
